ai.literal: South Kumari, north great mountain, / east and west oceans as boundaries, / hills, mountains, forests, and countries / uniting to speak your path, / removing evil, straightening the scepter, / doing what is due, performing with impartiality, / sweetly rolled bright wheel / of those who ruled entirely, O protector of their lineage! / Screw-pine bearing fruit with bent bunches, / wide fields with mountains as fences, / moonlight-like sand in the wide seaside grove, / upon the clear backwaters, with bright flowers, / O warrior who slays, of the cool Thondi people! / Not considering the weight of the great pit, / trapped inside a deep pit, / having pride, strength, and might, / a killer male elephant with matured tusks, / shaking its position, destroying the pit, / joins together as its herd rejoices; / like that, you experienced difficult might / and great distress, to the joy of many, / but went elsewhere to your flourishing inheritance, / and speaking highly in the midst of many, / 'The high land that exists, / and the excellent vessels obtained, / can be acquired if we win his heart,' some say, / 'The lofty flags on the joints of the walls, / and the wide fortress with thick ramparts, / we shall lose and abide, now we, / because he looked with great anger,' others say, / O you who begin the submission of other kings, / praising your strength and fame, / I have come to see you, O lord! / Confusing like gathered clouds, many shields, like mountains / vast many elephants where honeybees gather, / swelling to the fear of enemies, like the ocean / the army striving for rainwater, without ceasing, / making the heads of serpents with poison-filled fangs tremble, / with a drum roaring like thunder, / O king of the westerners with limitless generosity!
ai.translation: O protector of the lineage of those ancient kings who ruled the entire land bounded by Kumari in the south, the great Himalayas in the north, and the oceans in the east and west, where hills, mountains, forests, and countries united in submission under a righteous scepter that removed evil and ruled with sweet impartiality! O warrior of the cool seaside town of Thondi, with its wide fields fenced by mountains, screw-pines with heavy fruit-laden branches, moonlight-like sandy shores, and bright flowers blooming over clear backwaters! Just like a mighty, proud male elephant with sharp tusks that falls into a deep pit, but breaks free by destroying the pit to rejoin its rejoicing herd, you too overcame great captivity and distress to the joy of your subjects, returning to claim your flourishing inheritance. Hearing of your return, rival kings speak in two ways: some say, 'If we can win his favor, we can regain our high lands and excellent treasures,' while others say, 'He has looked upon us with great anger; we shall surely lose our high-walled fortresses and thick ramparts.' O lord, I have come to see you and praise your strength and fame! You possess an endless army with shields that look like dark clouds, mountain-like elephants surrounded by bees, and a vast host like the ocean. With your war drums roaring like thunder, making even the fanged serpents in the underworld tremble, you rule as the generous king of the western lands!
ai.modern: தெற்கே குமரிமுனையும், வடக்கே இமயமலையும், கிழக்கிலும் மேற்கிலும் கடல்களும் எல்லையாகக் கொண்ட இந்நிலப்பரப்பில் உள்ள குன்றுகளும், மலைகளும், காடுகளும், நாடுகளும் ஒன்றுபட்டு உனக்கு அடங்கி வழிமொழியுமாறு, தீமைகளைக் களைந்து, செங்கோலைச் செலுத்தி, நடுவுநிலைமையோடு ஆட்சிபுரிந்த முன்னோர்களின் வழியில் வந்த காவலனே! தாழைகள் நிறைந்த வயல்களையும், குளிர்ந்த தொண்டி நகரையும் உடையவனே! பெரிய குழியில் விழுந்த யானை அக்குழியைத் தகர்த்துத் தன் கூட்டத்தோடு இணைவது போல, நீ பகைவரிடம் சிறைப்பட்டுப் பின்னர் மீண்டு வந்து உனது அரியணையில் அமர்ந்தாய். உனது அருளைப் பெற்றால் இழந்த மண்ணையும் செல்வத்தையும் பெறலாம் என்று சிலரும், உனது சினத்திற்கு ஆளானால் எஞ்சிய கோட்டைகளையும் இழப்போம் என்று சிலரும் அஞ்சி உன்னை வணங்குகின்றனர். மேகம் போன்ற கேடயங்களும், மலை போன்ற யானைகளும், கடல் போன்ற சேனையும், இடி போன்ற முரசும் கொண்ட குடநாட்டின் வேந்தனே! உனது எல்லையற்ற கொடைத்தன்மையையும் ஆற்றலையும் கண்டு போற்ற யான் வந்துள்ளேன்.
ai.explanation: This poem is addressed to the Chera king Yanaikkatcey Mantaranjeral Irumporai by the poet Kurungoliyur Kilar. The poet praises the king's vast domain, which stretches from Cape Comorin in the south to the Himalayas in the north, bounded by the oceans. The central metaphor compares the king's temporary captivity and triumphant escape to a majestic elephant breaking free from a deep pit to rejoin its herd. Hearing of his return, rival kings react in two ways: some hope to win back their lost territories by gaining his favor, while others tremble in fear of his wrath and prepare to submit. The poet extols the king's formidable army, with its cloud-like shields, mountain-like elephants, and thunderous war drums, celebrating his limitless generosity and sovereign power.
